reason: The fibroblast conditions specify a developmental route for descendants toward supporting tissue.
expectation: The timed conditions will produce fibroblast-lineage cells that can help build supporting tissue.

alternatives.reason: The other specified route would prepare the muscle branch first.

effect: The fibroblast route produced cells with collagen RNA messages, suggesting amino acids can be used to make collagen.
reaction: The connection between selected genes and collagen messages is clear.
reason: The cells have collagen messages, and amino acids are the building blocks needed to make the protein.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to make collagen or a collagen precursor.

alternatives.reason: I could start the separate muscle branch first.

effect: The fibroblasts now produce procollagen in secretory vesicles, suggesting extracellular processing is next.
reaction: The distinction between intracellular procollagen production and extracellular processing is useful.
reason: Extracellular fluid contains processing enzymes and surrounds the living cells, making it a plausible place to build the supporting matrix.
expectation: The fibroblasts will secrete procollagen for extracellular processing into a supporting matrix.

alternatives.reason: I could begin the muscle branch instead.

effect: The fibroblasts secreted procollagen, which was processed into an extracellular matrix; living cells still need to be incorporated into the supporting tissue.
reaction: The separation between secretion and extracellular assembly is useful.
reason: Living fibroblasts together with their collagen-rich matrix are a plausible supporting tissue.
expectation: The cells and matrix will form a living supporting tissue.

alternatives.reason: I could prepare the separate muscle branch first.

effect: The fibroblasts and matrix formed living supporting tissue, completing that goal; the muscle branch remains.
reaction: The picture makes the relationship between cells and their surrounding matrix clear.
reason: The skeletal-muscle conditions specify the developmental route for the remaining goal.
expectation: The timed signals will produce muscle-forming progenitor cells.

effect: The muscle conditions produced committed cells with muscle-protein messages, but not mature fibres.
reaction: The distinction between lineage commitment and a mature fibre is clear.
reason: Amino acids can supply the building blocks for proteins specified by the muscle messages.
expectation: The cells will make muscle proteins and advance toward the muscle-forming goal.

effect: The muscle-lineage cells made muscle proteins and became separate, single-nucleus myoblasts, completing the goal without forming mature fibres.
reaction: The distinction between preparing myoblasts and producing a mature muscle fibre was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building living supporting tissue was most worthwhile: the sequence connected collagen messages to protein production, secretion, extracellular assembly and a tissue containing both cells and matrix.

leastWorthwhile.text: The parallel muscle branch repeated the signals-then-amino-acids pattern, although the comparison helped show how different messages yield different proteins.

surprise.text: The fibroblasts produced procollagen inside the cell before extracellular processing assembled collagen fibres; the resulting matrix alone was not yet the living tissue.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though terms such as mesenchymal progenitors, paraxial mesoderm and procollagen were not explained in the supplied prose or picture plans.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the separate myoblasts develop into mature muscle fibres, since this chapter deliberately stops short of fusion.
